Replay

Editor workbench

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Development boundaryChecks and current scope

Open dev/workbench.tscn, choose preview options in the inspector and press F6. ReplayWorkbench boots the actual main.tscn game in solo mode, waits for its normal identity/loadout/ready/start path, then submits development actions. The world, director, statuses, deaths, shops and renderer use the game's normal code. The original sibling game's workbench remains independent.

Inspector option Preview behavior
open_shop One short wave; repeatedly damage ordinary enemies through the normal death/credit/drop rules; grant 500 scrap and 20 cores
boss Spawn a Titan near the runner; it remains alive and holds the room in combat even when open_shop is selected
statuses Apply rally and chill, refreshing through the status/reaction rules every two seconds
hurt Apply half of the runner's maximum health as damage
jam Put the equipped gun into a valid jammed state with its configured clearing taps
kegs Spawn 0–12 props near the runner using the existing pool/action path
menu Open the Esc menu
wipe Down the solo runner and let the normal wipe/reset transition run
note Show the narrator notice
tally Open the live tally

The preview uses seed 1337, one wave, no automatic barrels and a 30-tick rest. open_shop selects three normal enemies; otherwise there are six. Timers keep running. The workbench is playable and a wipe eventually resets normally.

The vitals line remains visible during clear/shop states and shows health, ammunition, jam/reload state and active statuses. Tab opens the live per-player kill/damage/mend/scrap/core tally; releasing Tab closes it. Esc opens a menu with return, run-save, PNG selection and Quit controls in a dimmed, scrolling menu. The menu blocks local gameplay input while the session continues to simulate and receive traffic. A Room/client cannot use its save button to write an authority archive.

Development boundary#

The default game model refuses Dev_Spawn and Dev_Edit. A tool session must explicitly enable development, and the authority admits edits only from its own local playable seat. The scene supplies that opt-in. Setting the same flag in a remote client does not authorize its commands. A dedicated server without a local seat cannot issue these through the player-facing path.

Dev_Edit has a named Development payload: kind, target seat, amount and status. Godot helpers return a submitted action sequence, not an authority verdict: dev_hurt, dev_jam, dev_status, dev_grant_scrap, dev_grant_cores and dev_smite. Accepted actions use the existing action ledger, replay and archive machinery. Smite preserves bosses and props and uses ordinary damage/death rules; it does not assign the stage directly. Invalid quantities or targets fail before mutation, and counter overflow aborts the simulation transaction.

The scene disables profile persistence. Its save and spray paths are the separate user://workbench-run.replay and user://workbench-spray.png. Both the spray load path and its separate write destination are scoped to the workbench. Launch environment values are retained and restored when the workbench exits. Ordinary run/profile files are not preview output paths. The scene is intended for native editor F6; its code passes WASM checking, but browser workbench execution is not claimed.

Checks and current scope#

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/workbench_run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_scrapyard/development_run.sh

The first test exercises the panels/status/jam preview, a boss that prevents clear, and a normal wipe. It checks action confirmation, UI content, key transitions, continued simulation with blocked movement, status refresh, environment restoration and clean shutdown. A rendered capture is retained in the workbench evidence. The second test rejects all six edits from a real client, accepts the host's grants to that client and compares both complete world hashes afterward.

The audio/settings layer supplies volume, shake, fullscreen, and spray-preview controls. Full visual/listening parity and paired human review remain required work. This is not a claim of full Scrapyard feature parity.

The action extension introduced content ...3043; audio event details introduced ...3044; cast paths introduced ...3046, followed by dash actions at ...3047. Gameplay protocol 7 and checkpoint layout 4 were unchanged by these transitions. The explicit save importer maps content-42/43/44/45 archives, including pending accepted/refused requests, while preserving the complete world and image payloads.
